finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id performs no authorization check: authorized() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any project by ID.
finding.source: req.params.id (URL path) with the attacker's session supplying req.user

trace.note: DELETE /projects/:id route registered with no authorization middleware
project loaded by attacker-supplied ID with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) called but its boolean return value is discarded, so nothing throws or blocks

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 has correct logic but is not enforced; authorize() at api.js:4-10 would throw 403 but is not used on this route; no auth middleware in this file; no null check on project (nonexistent ID yields TypeError, not 404). Precondition: caller is authenticated (or req.user is set) and knows a project ID they do not own; if the mounting app does not gate this router, it is reachable unauthenticated. Fix: call authorize(req.user, project) at api.js:18 or return 403 when authorized() is false.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at api.js:18 as a bare statement, so it enforces nothing. authorize() at api.js:4-10 (which throws 403) is defined but never called on the DELETE route (api.js:16-21). No auth or ownership middleware is registered on that route. The directory contains only api.js, so no mounting app gating is visible.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:16-21 calls authorized() at line 18 and discards its boolean result, so the delete at line 19 runs for any project ID regardless of ownership; the only caller-side requirement is that req.user is set, and the trace matches the code exactly.
